Empirically tested CodeQL's suggested pump ('Paragraf 0 ' + repeated double-spaces) up to 320,000 chars: clean 2x-for-2x (O(n)) growth, no blowup.

TOPIC_PATTERN = r'TENTANG\s+(.+?)(?=DENGAN RAHMAT|Menimbang|Mengingat|$)' with DOTALL. The lazy .+? can always terminate at '$' (end of string), so there is no reachable total-failure case forcing exhaustive backtracking — worst case is a single linear scan to end. Empirically tested CodeQL's pump ('TENTANG ' + repeated double-spaces) up to 320,000 chars: clean 2x-for-2x growth.

Same DOTALL lazy-.+?-terminates-at-$ shape as #7776: once the literal phrase is found, the match extends to the next \n or end of string in one linear pass and (being global re.sub) consumes past all further phrase repetitions in the same match. Empirically tested with the exact CodeQL pump (phrase repeated up to 51,200 times, ~1.5MB) both with and without interspersed newlines: clean linear growth (ratio ~4x for 4x input), no blowup.

This local pattern has no literal-after-an-anchor-with-\s*-in-between ambiguity like PASAL_PATTERN — matches only start where a literal '(' + digit occurs, and .+? (DOTALL) always reaches the '$' fallback. Empirically tested with both space-padding and newline-padding pumps up to 160,000 chars: consistently ~0.0000-0.0002s, no growth.

EMAIL_PATTERN = r'(?i)(?<![A-Z0-9._%+-])[A-Z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z]{2,}(?![A-Z0-9._%+-])'. The negative lookbehind before the user-part quantifier means any restart position immediately preceded by another identifier char is rejected in O(1) — this prunes almost every one of the O(n) candidate restart positions that would otherwise each cost O(n). Directly tested THIS pattern (with the lookaround) with both .search() and .sub() on a guaranteed-no-match string ('a@'+'a'*n+'%') up to 128,000 chars: clean linear growth in both cases (0.0037s at 128000), confirming the lookbehind neutralizes the theoretical ambiguity. Contrast with #7409 below, which is the same core email shape MINUS the lookaround and IS exploitable.
